questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: London is such a big, international city which really appealed to me and I was sure that there was so much to see and do! Moreover, I was pretty sure the academic level would be more fitting than other destinations and I have family members living in the city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was everything I hoped for and I have made such good friends and really gotten to know the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy as there was some introductory meetings and a lot of e-mails sent out from the university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a lot of e-mails before arrival which also included invitations to introduction meetings where the uni gave a lot of information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The university has different locations around London - some close to a campus and others not. They differ in prices so my strategy was to look for the cheaper options but I also found that the location really matters a lot. So look at a map and situate the different accommodation options. Also try to get into the accommodation portal as quick as possible as they are gone pretty fast. If you don't manage to get something immediately, then keep on checking the portal as places keep on showing up - that was how I got my place.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The place I lived at had a shared kitchen for the flat I lived in which I shared with nine other people. It was a bit dirty but for half a year it was manageable.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I found accommodation through the university and was very happy about it because my location was really, really central and since it is very difficult to find housing in London. I came a little late into the uni's accommodation portal and consequently, there were no available rooms at first but I just kept on checking the portal and eventually, something showed up on the portal which I then got. I think it was easier to just go with student accommodation because I didn't know the city and areas that well and because it was actually a good price for the location I got - even though London is just insanely expensive. I lived at Stamford Street Apartments which I can really recommend since it was the second cheapest and the location was amazing so I could walk a lot to the destinations I needed to get to. Also Wolfson House is the cheapest and has a really good location - but of course it depends on which campus you have to spend most time at. Tip: Look up the different locations at the uni's website in advance before the accommodation portal opens and figure out which place you want to aim for, taking into account both the prices and locations. Try to get into the portal as quick as possible and if you don't get anything keep on checking anyways as things will appear later as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very happy which the location and the place - but the kitchen was very dirty as times which was not the nicest. Despite that, I would really recommend it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It took quite some time before the registrations opened because you had to fill out a looong document which a lot of priorities and had to check if the courses overlapped yourself - but as soon as the registrations opened it was easy as you just send the document by email. I got all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write an e-mail to the university if you had any questions and they where very fast at replying.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wished for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to fill in the document with priorities in advance so you are ready to send it the second the registration opens.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had level 7 courses which was the only level I could choose being a MA student. I found the level very similar to that of my home institution.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching is a bit different in England. My classes were shorter (1 hour lecture, 1 hour seminar), there were fewer people in the classes and the seminars are a lot more interactive than in Denmark.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
7AAON006 - Capitalism, liberalism and democracy
7AAON004 - Foreign Policies of the European Union
7AAON003 - European Identities and the EU
7AAON036 - The European Union & Global Capitalism

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend the "European Identities and the EU" module as it was very interesting and the teacher Russell Foster good and funny. The class isn't that difficult but it is interesting. Also I really liked the Foreign Policies of the European Union.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It is a bit surprising how expensive London actually is. So the prices on food and so on were surprising and you just always end up using more money than you think.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Museums are free which is really cool. Coffee is also cheaper than in Denmark. Groceries are pretty expensive (at least where I lived) and train rides are also expensive. I can recommend getting a National Railcard (I had the 16-25 years old one) where you get a discount on all the train tickets you buy and also you can connect it to your oyster card and get a discount for the tube and busses. It costs 30 pounds I think but you have really quickly saved that - especially if you plan on travelling around in the UK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a gym at the place I lived and they offered yoga classes, pilates classes and circuit training and much more.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of lunches and social events (especially in the beginning) and then a lot of athletic activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going to a lot of events in the first weeks because a lot of exchange students did and I found a lot of friends there.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend going on trips around the UK: Bath, Bristol, Oxford, Cambridge, Cotswolds, Brighton, Canterbury, White Cliffs of Dover, Seven Sisters, Liverpool, Manchester. Also I went on a trip to Scotland for 8 days after uni was over which was amazing!

Moreover, I can really recommend just exploring London. It is so big that you never really run out of areas or things to see. My favorite places are probably Hampstead (Hampstead Heath and Primrose Hill), Bermondsey, Shoreditch.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - the UK culture is not too different but still different enough that it is interesting.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend the events in the first week and try to talk to people in classes. Or join a local sports club.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think the most challenging was to figure out how things were done academically - but it was not that hard and the teachers were all really sweet and helpful.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love the pub culture and just London and British people in general.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Remember that the exams are transferred as passed or failed so don't stress too much about school.
- Try to get accommodation that is pretty central as London is big and commuting very expensive.
- If you are doubtful about anything academically go to the professor's office hours.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think I have covered the most important.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That I have had more time than I normally have because I didn't have a job on the side so I have really just have half a year where I could explore, make friends and become much better at English :)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Figuring out the level academically and what was expected. My advice is: Try not to use too much time on it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
